title: Deep Exploration of the Immunopeptidome of a Pancreatic Cancer Cell Line Panc1: Implications for Clinical Immunopeptidomics and Immunotherapy (SWATH-DIA datasets)
projectDescription: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), with its devastating prognosis and limited treatment options, necessitates innovative therapeutic strategies. T-cell-based immunotherapy has shown promise for various cancers, including PDAC. Thus, a comprehensive understanding of the HLA-peptidome in PDAC is essential to pave the way for the effective design of immunotherapy and other interventions. In this study, we employed off-line high-pH reverse-phase (HPH-RP) fractionation of peptides extracted from immunoaffinity purified HLA class I molecules isolated from the surface of Panc1 cells in the absence and presence of cytokine stimulation. We demonstrate that this strategy is a relatively simple and rapid technique that significantly expands the depth of coverage of the PDAC immunopeptidome using data-dependent acquisition strategies and allowing the identification of more potentially actionable peptide antigens. Whilst cell lines provide an abundant source of material for immunopeptidomics analysis, clinical samples and biopsies from pancreatic cancer patients typically involve much smaller amounts of material. Thus, we performed a proof of concept study and demonstrated that immunopeptidome characterization was feasible from cell pellets of only 1 million cells (equivalent to approximately 1mg of tissue), using a spectral library generated from the HPH-RP fractionated material and the ZenoSWATH DIA-MS workflow on the SCIEX 7600 ZenoToF system. These studies form the basis for future clinical translational immunopeptidomics approaches to screen tumor antigen presentation in PDAC biopsies and provide new opportunities for immune-based therapies.
sampleProcessingProtocol: HLA ligand isolation: Cell pellets were lysed using an IGEPAL-based lysis buffer consisting of 0.5% IGEPAL CA630 (Sigma), 50 mM Tris HCL, 150 mM NaCl, and 1x cOmplete Protease inhibitor (Roche). Lysates were centrifuged at 4oC, 13K rpm, for 10 min, then passed over protein A agarose (PAA) beads (pre-column) to remove non-specific binders. Next, PAA-bound W6/32 was used to immunoprecipitate the HLA molecules as described (Purcell et al. 2019 Nature Protocols). Using 10% acetic acid, antibodies, HLA molecules, and their cargos were eluted from the PAA, and the eluates passed through a centrifugal 5KDa molecular weight cut-off filter (Millipore); the 5KDa filter flowthrough contains the peptides and the retentate consists of antibodies, β2M, and HLA heavy chain proteins. The peptides in the flowthrough were concentrated and desalted using OMIX C18 pipette tips (Agilent). After centrifugal evaporation in a SpeedVac, dried peptides were reconstituted in loading buffer (aqueous 0.1% formic acid + 2% Acetonitrile) with the addition of 11 iRT (GL-Biochem, Shanghai) peptides at 25 fmole/ul per peptide and transferred to MS vials. High-pH reversed-phased (HPH-RP) fractionation of HLA-peptides: HLA-peptides eluted in 10% acetic acid were fractionated using an HPH-RP fractionation stage column kit (ThermoScientific Ref #84868). Approximately 85% of the eluate from 3.5x108 pellets of Panc1 (equivalent to an eluate from 3x108 cells) was fractionated based on the manufacturer’s protocol (i.e. 8 fractions eluted with 0.1% Triethylamine and 5%, 7.5%, 10%, 12.5%, 15%, 17.5%, 20%, or 50% Acetonitrile). The fractions were frozen and dried by a centrifugal evaporation unit. Without further desalting, peptides were reconstituted in the MS loading buffer with iRT peptide standards as mentioned above, transferred to MS sample vials, and queued on the mass spectrometer. Data-dependent acquisition of mass spectra: Spectra from DDA-LC-MS/MS runs of the HLA-bound peptides were acquired on a SCIEX 7600 ZenoTOF equipped with an ACQUITY M Class UHPLC system (Waters) in a direct injection mode. The mobile phases A and B consisted of aqueous 0.1% formic acid and 100% Acetonitrile with 0.1% formic acid, respectively. For all of the samples, HLA-peptides were dissolved in 12ul MS loading buffer with iRT peptides spiked in, and 2ul was injected onto an Aurora ELITE SX 150 mm x 75µm nanoflow UHPLC column (IonOpticks). The HLA-bound peptide mixture was separated with a linear 45-minute gradient of 2-30% Acetonitrile at 300 nL/min flow rate in a total run time of 85 min. Following the TOF MS scan, the top 45 most intense ions with a charge state between +1 to +5 and an intensity greater than 100 counts per second (cps) were selected for collision-induced dissociation (CID) fragmentation and MS/MS spectra acquisition, with Zenotrap pulsing (threshold=100000 cps) and no dynamic background subtraction. The accumulation time for the TOF MS and TOF MS/MS experiments were 150 ms and 20 ms, respectively. The collision energy (CE) of the CID reaction was calculated automatically based on the dynamic CE settings in the SCIEX operating system. Variable Window ZenoSWATH Data-independent acquisition of mass spectra: The same LC separation method was used for the ZenoSWATH acquisitions. The variable-window ZenoSWATH (vwZSW) isolation windows were designed based on the precursor m/z distribution of Panc1 HLA peptides acquired in the DDA runs and the “SWATH Variable Window Calculator V1.2” Excel sheet. The method has 78 variable overlapping windows between 350 to 1250 m/z, with a 7 m/z minimum size and 1 m/z overlaps (further details are available in supplementary materials). The accumulation time for the TOF MS and TOF MS/MS experiments was 100 ms and 13 ms, respectively, and the total cycle time is calculated as 1.508 s. The Zenotrap pulsing threshold was set at 100000 cps.
dataProcessingProtocol: DDA .wiff files were converted to mzML format using msConvertGUI in ProteoWizard 3.0.22189 with a vendor-provided peak-picking algorithm. Datasets were searched in FragPipe 21.1 with the MSFragger 4.0 search engine [11-13], ionQuant 1.10.12 [14], and Philosopher 5.1.0 [15]. Search parameters are summarized in Table 1. Peptides were quantified by label-free quantification (without match-between-runs), and MSBooster [16] was employed to enhance the identifications. The Homo sapiens reviewed protein sequences database (SwissProt) was downloaded from UniProt on 2022.09.30. Two protein entries were added to the database for KRAS (P01116) G12D and TP53 (P04637) P72R and R273H mutations, known shared mutations present in the Panc1 cell line based on the COSMIC database [17]. For HLA-peptidomics experiments, only the 11 iRT peptides, Bovine-sourced contaminants, and Immunoglobulin G-binding protein A (UniProt ID = P02976) of Staphylococcus aureus were added to the SwissProt sequences. This set of contaminants is used because cells are cultured in bovine serum-supplemented media; also, eluates might get contaminated with non-specific fragments of Protein A during the immunoprecipitation. To generate the spectral library with FragPipe [18], the same MSFragger config is employed, but the MS1 LFQ (ionQuant) tab is disabled, and the DDA files are imported without setting the experimental groups. Settings for the Spectral Library tab are found in Table S1. The DIA files were searched with DIA-NN [19] 1.8.2 beta 8 using the HPH-RP Deep spectral library. The parameters for the search are provided in Table S2.
